content: Indication-specific dosing for kola nut (Cola nitida) is not well-established, and there is no typical dosage recommended. It is possibly effective for alleviating physical and mental fatigue, though evidence remains limited. Fluconazole has been shown to increase the levels of kola nut in the body by reducing its metabolism. However, the clinical significance of this interaction is considered minor and remains uncertain. Similarly, grapefruit can also increase kola nut levels by decreasing its metabolism, but this interaction is also classified as minor with unknown significance. Tachycardia (an abnormally fast heart rate) has been noted as a potential adverse effect, though specific frequency data is not available. Regarding pregnancy, kola nut falls under a general category of acceptability. Controlled studies in pregnant women have not demonstrated evidence of fetal risk. However, specific pregnancy and lactation safety schedules are not available.
